title: Exchange preserves normalized global generators and detects invertibility
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and let
$$\begin{array}{ccc}X'&\xrightarrow{v}&X\\ a'\downarrow&&\downarrow a\\ B'&\xrightarrow{g}&B\end{array}$$
be a cartesian square of schemes [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Work with constant-ring etale module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. Let $L$ be a sheaf of $A$-modules on $B$, placed in degree zero, put $F=a^*L$ and $F'=v^*F=a'^*g^*L$, and let
$$b:g^*Ra_*F\longrightarrow Ra'_*F'$$
be the specified derived exchange [sbc-def-base-change-map], using the canonical inverse-image square identification. Let $\eta_a(L)$ and $\eta_{a'}(g^*L)$ be the adjunction units. Then, after that square identification,
$$b\circ g^*\eta_a(L)=\eta_{a'}(g^*L).$$
For $q\geq0$, let $e_a^q$ send a global class to its Leray edge section in $\Gamma(B,R^qa_*F)$, equivalently a global injective-resolution cocycle to its class in the direct-image cohomology sheaf. For every $x\in H^q(X,F)$, the following equality of sections on $B'$ holds:
$$\mathcal H^q(b)\bigl(g^*e_a^q(x)\bigr)=e_{a'}^q(v^*x),$$
where $v^*$ is the canonical cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] and $\mathcal H^q(g^*Ra_*F)=g^*R^qa_*F$. This is equality for the actual module-derived exchange, under the canonical module/abelian comparisons, not merely existence of a morphism taking one generator to the other.

In particular, suppose the degree-zero units $L\to R^0a_*F$ and $g^*L\to R^0a'_*F'$ are isomorphisms, and that all cohomology sheaves of both direct images vanish outside degrees $0,1$. If $x\in H^1(X,F)$ has edge section generating an isomorphism $A_B\to R^1a_*F$, and $v^*x$ similarly gives an isomorphism $A_{B'}\to R^1a'_*F'$, then $b$ is an isomorphism. The same conclusion holds when both direct images have cohomology only in degree zero, without a degree-one class. No finite-type hypothesis on $g$ is needed.

proof.text: Prove compatibility of the constant single-degree comparison with composition using leftDerivedUpperStar_map_singleFunctor_comp and Scheme.upperStarConstantSheafIso_comp. Cancelling the composition isomorphisms gives genericConstantIso_square. Naturality and unit_mateEquiv give adjunct_mate; compatibility of the actual exchange with shifts gives shifted_adjunct_mate. Apply this to the adjoint of the global class, and use the constant square equality to identify its source with the pulled-back constant sheaf. Apply H^0 and the shift comparison via iso_homology_class. Naturality of singleFunctorCompHomologyFunctorIso identifies the remaining source comparison. This proves relativeKummerExchange_edge directly for the specified module-derived exchange. The private calculation is made over a general abelian monoidal coefficient category and any object K, then specialized to ModuleCat A and the free rank-one object. The equation higher_eq records only reassociation of the canonical composites. The constructions and all four proofs are made over a general coefficient category, and the public module-valued declarations specialize them. One shared genericConstantIso fixes the constant/single comparison throughout and avoids repeated kernel conversions of concrete derived instances. The generic constant-square cancellation is proved once in arbitrary categories. The constant-square and shifted-adjunct calculations are local to kummer_edge_naturality, so that the kernel checks their combination without repeated concrete conversions. Public module-valued result abbreviations specialize the complete generic theorems; no proposition or mathematical construction changes.

proof.text: Apply DerivedCategory.isIso_iff in the ordinary unbounded derived category. At degree zero, functoriality of the exact-pullback homology comparison transfers invertibility of the first unit; the mate-unit equality and invertibility of the second unit then give invertibility of H^0(exchange). At degree one, relativeKummerExchange_edge identifies the composite of the pulled-back invertible generator and kummerExchangeHigherMap with the invertible target generator. Cancel the generator and the canonical homology comparison. In every other degree exact pullback preserves IsZero and every map between zero objects is invertible. For the degree-zero-only theorem use the same degree-zero computation and the vanishing hypothesis in all other degrees. No boundedness, geometric finiteness or torsion assumption is introduced.
